units.headline: Record lookup errors no longer fail Track; item tracked without owner
units.summary: loadMetadata now drops the error from getRecord and always returns success for KindRecord items. Track no longer reports any lookup failure. Transient ones (timeouts, connection errors) are dropped too, not only FORBIDDEN, so those items are stored with no inventory owner.
focus: Transient errors (deadline, connect failure) are swallowed along with FORBIDDEN replies
Track never reloads metadata, so an item tracked during an outage keeps no owner
Callers of Track that relied on its error to retry

issues.title: Transient lookup failures permanently lose the record owner
issues.failure_scenario: Inventory times out (context deadline of requestTimeout) during Track. Before this change Track returned the error and the caller could retry. Now the item is stored with record.Owner == "" and it.Owner is never refined, because nothing re-runs loadMetadata for a tracked item.

units.reason: Changes error propagation: Track now succeeds on every kind of lookup failure, including transient ones.

units.headline: New tests for client error/success caching and loader fallback
units.summary: New tests cover the per-key error cache and its TTL, success caching, isErrorReply wrapping, and loadMetadata falling back on lookup errors. They use injected get/now hooks and change no production code.
units.reason: New test file only; it cannot affect production behavior.
